No SKU ≥15 kg exists in the whole catalogue. Largest atta pack is 10 kg (Aashirvaad 10 Kg, ₹74,235). Canteen/mess atta moves as 1 kg packs and loose kg transferred and booked as Consumption at Ary G Canteen — there is no sellable institutional bag or quotation SKU

LIKE '%bran%' → only rice-bran oil and bran bread; '%chokar%'/'%chokkar%' → 0 rows

surprises: Loose / repacked by-the-kilo is the whole category, not a sideline: Atta 1 Kg (12,500 kg @ exactly ₹40/kg), Rice 1 Kg (9,800 kg @ ₹68/kg), Rice_L, Atta_L, Dalia_L and Besan_L together are ₹20.64 L of the lane's ₹32.93 L — 63% of 12-month sales — sold in Kgs out of the 'Basement' warehouse. The ideal list called loose atta 'highest-margin line'; at ARY it is simply the business.

Nothing in ARY's 21,500 SKUs is packed 15 kg or bigger. The institutional atta/rice/maida bag does not exist as a sellable item. Instead the canteens are fed 1 kg retail packs transferred in and booked as internal Consumption: Raja Maida 1 Kg was bought at ₹62,451 (1,960 kg) with ₹0 POS sales, and the Stock buckets show ~4,000 kg consumed at Ary G Canteen / Ary Lite / Ary Apple A Day. Same shape for Sunil Ararot 1 Kg (₹31,900 bought, ₹120 sold), Gobind Maida 1 Kg (₹4,482 / ₹0) and Yumirra Pasta 5 Kg (₹10,724 / ₹0).

Therefore a sales-only read of this category is wrong: four of the biggest purchase lines look like dead stock and are actually the mess kitchen. Any assortment decision here has to read Stock.Cons, not just SaleDetail.

Dalia_L (2,200 kg, ₹81,400 — the lane's 5th biggest line) is filed under product group 'Others → subgroup Custard', so it is invisible to any report grouped by 'Rice & Other Grains'. Its packed sibling Rajdhani Daliya 1 Kg (₹1,26,453) is correctly filed.

Group 143 'Rice & Other Grains' is a dumping ground: it holds 15 pasta SKUs, Jivo chia/flax/pumpkin/basil/quinoa seeds, sliced black olives, green cardamom, til/kalonji/alsi, mixed dal and kulath dal — roughly 28 SKUs that are neither rice nor a grain, and they carry ₹1.0 L+ of the group total.

Spelling breaks search, and one misspelling hides the only SKU of its kind: the sole jowar atta is 'Zowar Atta 250 Gm' (LIKE '%jowar%' returns Kurkure snacks only). Also 'Bamati Rice' and an empty 'Miada' subgroup beside 'Maida', 'Pulses & Lenitils', 'Fortune Beson', 'Daawat Basmari'.

A 57% dormant tail: 138 of 242 SKUs in groups 110+143 had zero sales in 12 months — all 7 Patanjali attas, both Amul Organic attas, Samrat, Purn Adhaar, Umang Bhog, Silver Coin, 9 of 11 poha SKUs, 11 of 22 oats SKUs, 10 of 15 maida SKUs. The listed catalogue is roughly twice the size of the real one.

The fasting-flour set is half-built in a place where it should be strongest: kuttu sells (₹2,850) and samak rice sells (₹3,980), but singhara atta has sat at zero for 12 months with zero purchases, and rajgira does not exist. The vrat customer is demonstrably real and is being served incompletely.

Sattu is one SKU that sold six packs in a year (last 2025-09-17) and chana/missi atta does not exist at all — so both the Bihar/UP student summer-drink line and the traditional diabetic roti line are effectively absent, while no branded diabetic atta exists to substitute.

No chakki or grinding service SKU exists anywhere, and no whole wheat grain either — so ARY buys pre-ground loose atta and carries the full hill-humidity spoilage risk on flour rather than holding grain. That is the single largest structural gap the ideal list identified, and the data confirms it.
